title: These App Store hidden gems prove there’s still room for great software in the AI era
excerpt: Despite predictions that AI agents could make traditional apps obsolete, developers are shipping new software faster than ever. From smarter bookmarking tools and neighborhood marketplaces to digital pen pals and nature journals, here are the latest App Store finds worth adding to your Home Screen.
content_html:
Apps are back, or maybe they never left in the first place.

While some people debate whether people will shift away from apps as AI agents make accessing online services more efficient, we’ve found the App Store to be alive and well, with a recent explosion of fun, creative, and innovative tools, experiences, and other indie efforts.

Some of the more recent launches may be attributed to the rise of AI coding, which has enabled people to ship software more quickly, and allowed novices to participate in the app ecosystem. According to one report, new app launches have soared in 2026, with worldwide new app releases up 60% year-over-year as of the first quarter across both the Apple App Store and Google Play. On Apple’s iOS store alone, that figure was an even higher 80%.

While there’s valid concern that vibe-coded apps in particular could be cluttering the App Store with lower-quality content, there are plenty of interesting apps worth exploring, and those that resonate with consumers will rise to the top. Many also use AI under the hood to perform their magic — they’re just not promoted as being “AI-powered.”

Below is our latest collection of App Store hidden gems, which we’ve added to our Home Screen. You can also visit TechCrunch’s prior app round-ups, like our looks at next-generation social apps, Apple Watch, and iPad productivity tools, and apps for digitally decluttering your life.

Albo

Albo (previously Sortd, but not that Sortd) is an excellent tool for anyone who regularly bookmarks content from social media, then promptly forgets about it. With Albo, the idea is that you’ll instead share the link to the TikTok, Instagram Reel, YouTube video, or other website to the app. Albo will then automatically pull the details from the post and categorize and save the idea for you. That post and its notes will remain available in Albo, even if the original content creator deletes their post or video at some point in the future.

The app works with a variety of social apps, including Pinterest, X, LinkedIn, Threads, Reddit, and Facebook, plus browsers like Chrome and Safari. You can also add screenshots to Albo.

This makes it easy to save any sort of online inspiration for easy access, whether that’s travel ideas, local spots to try, movie or shows to watch, books to read, recipes to cook, or workouts to do. Your collections can also be shared with friends.

Albo hails from the London-based app studio The Feel Good Project, which focuses on tech that makes users feel inspired and satisfied instead of drained by doomscrolling.

The app is free to use with advanced features available via subscription. We didn’t love how heavy-handed it was in pushing the trial subscription during onboarding, however.

Available on iOS and Google Play.

Coop

The recent parasite outbreak in the U.S. has people thinking more carefully about where their food comes from. Buying from local growers and bakers may be the safer option — and better for the community — but not everyone has time to make it to the farmer’s market over the weekend.

Coop‘s app offers an alternative through its neighborhood marketplace, where you can buy real handmade and homegrown items from the people near you, even from the farmhouse down the road that offers fresh eggs, or a neighbor willing to barter their items for yours. The idea is to allow commerce to stay local, while helping people turn their own garden, field, or craft into an additional income stream.

On Coop, you can browse and discover nearby sellers, follow your favorites, see how far they are from you, and purchase from them via the app’s Stripe integration. The seller then receives the order and prepares it for pickup.

Available on iOS and Google Play.

PI.FYI by Perfectly Imperfect

A colorful and somewhat chaotic app, PI.FYI, promises to bring back the “old internet,” where you found recommendations through a network of friends, not algorithms. Having emerged from a cult newsletter, the app has been around for a couple of years, but still feels fresh and modern and very much like the alternative to social media it aims become.

In PI.FYI, you can track what you’re into, share your taste, and browse by category or “scenes,” like music, whimsy, retro, and literature, to find your community, read interesting articles, make lists, gather local recommendations, and play games with friends. The app exudes a retro vibe itself, as if it were built when the internet was a little less polished, too.

Available on iOS and Google Play.

Lettre

OK, it might not be as fun as sharing a letter via pigeon post, but the app for pen pals, Lettre, also embraces the fun of snail mail in a digital format. This letter-writing app lets you start new friendships with pen pals around the world, discovered through the app, or with anyone whose email address you already know. Unfortunately, letters are sent digitally through the app or email for now, but the company’s FAQ suggests it is considering a postal mail option for the future, which would be so much fun.

Available on iOS only.

Sofa Time

While not a brand-new app, Sofa Time is one of several that is picking up where the recently shuttered TV Time app left off. The app has an easy-to-use, uncluttered interface for tracking the movies and TV shows you’re watching, organizing your watchlist, discovering what to stream next, and getting reminders about new releases.

While Sofa Time’s commenting section doesn’t yet rival TV Time’s forums, the app’s social elements leave room for the community to grow, as it supports the ability to react with a GIF or image alongside your text, and includes built-in translation features to support a global audience.

Available on iOS and Google Play.

ThingsBook

ThingsBook, a new writing-focused app from South Korean internet giant Naver’s U.S. subsidiary, is hardly an indie effort, but it’s an interesting premise for what the future of social media could look like. Instead of doomscrolling, ThingsBook offers a flexible space where you can capture what you care about, whether that’s through journaling, logging ideas, or collecting things like books, travels, meals, hobbies, and goals into structured lists you can revisit and expand.

The company explains that the app’s purpose is not to focus on “fleeting trends” but to become a “living record of who you are and what you love.”

Available on iOS and Google Play.

Pressed Petals

App or artistic project? Pressed Petals is both. An indie effort from designer Cynthia Chen, the app turns the photos of flowers you find on your walks into a pressed specimen, like one you’d find in a “vintage botanical journal.” The app automatically saves the location where you spotted the flower, and the date and time, turning your nature walks into interactive experiences. It also identifies the flower by name, both its scientific name and its common name.

You can try the app to press two flowers for free, then pay a one-time fee of $4.99 to unlock the full experience. This could be a fun app for luring your little ones outside, as it gives them something else to do beyond the hike itself.

Available on iOS only.

Moods Faster

We’re suckers for single-purpose apps that are built well. Moods Faster by Nick Leith is a perfect example, as it offers a way to log your moods for tracking in Apple Health in just two taps — one to select the mood and a second to save it.

You can choose between logging your current mood or your overall mood for the day, and can also optionally add information about the context and emotions you’re experiencing at the time of logging. In the settings, you can pick between different color schemes for your moods, though some are paywalled.

At $1.95 per month, it’s a reasonably priced subscription for anyone who regularly tracks their moods and emotions for mental health purposes.

Available on iOS only.

Activate Fitness

Originally pitched as a way to encourage kids to exercise, Activate Fitness has recently expanded its screen-time-earning app to include the whole family, which, frankly, makes it better. (The kids will just hate their parents for using this otherwise. Plus, it could turn outdoor time or exercise into a dreaded chore in kids’ minds, which defeats the purpose.)

For adults, the app could allow you to accomplish your own personal goals, like no doomscrolling until you get your steps in for the day.

Available on iOS only.

This post was originally published on July 28, 2026.

content_html_zh:
应用程序又回来了，或者也许它们从一开始就从未离开过。

虽然有些人争论随着人工智能代理使访问在线服务更加高效，人们是否会放弃应用程序，但我们发现应用程序商店仍然充满活力，最近有大量有趣、有创意和创新的工具、体验和其他独立的努力。

最近的一些发布可能归因于人工智能编码的兴起，它使人们能够更快地发布软件，并允许新手参与应用程序生态系统。 一份报告显示，2026 年新应用发布量猛增，截至第一季度，Apple App Store 和 Google Play 的全球新应用发布量同比增长 60%。 仅在苹果的 iOS 商店中，这个数字就高达 80%。

尽管人们担心振动编码的应用程序可能会在应用程序商店中充斥着低质量的内容，但仍有许多有趣的应用程序值得探索，而那些与消费者产生共鸣的应用程序将跻身榜首。 许多人还在幕后使用人工智能来施展魔法——他们只是没有被宣传为“人工智能驱动”。

以下是我们最新的 App Store 隐藏瑰宝合集，我们已将其添加到主屏幕中。 您还可以访问 TechCrunch 之前的应用综述，例如我们对下一代社交应用、Apple Watch 和 iPad 生产力工具以及用于以数字方式整理您的生活的应用的看法。

Albo

Albo（以前是 Sortd，但不是现在的 Sortd）对于那些经常在社交媒体上为内容添加书签，然后很快就忘记的人来说是一个出色的工具。 对于 Albo，我们的想法是，您可以将 TikTok、Instagram Reel、YouTube 视频或其他网站的链接分享到应用程序。 然后 Albo 会自动从帖子中提取详细信息，并为您分类和保存想法。 即使原始内容创建者在未来某个时候删除了他们的帖子或视频，该帖子及其注释仍将在 Albo 中保留。

该应用程序可与各种社交应用程序配合使用，包括 Pinterest、X、LinkedIn、Threads、Reddit 和 Facebook，以及 Chrome 和 Safari 等浏览器。 您还可以将屏幕截图添加到 Albo。

这使得您可以轻松保存任何类型的在线灵感以供轻松访问，无论是旅行创意、值得尝试的当地景点、要看的电影或节目、要阅读的书籍、要烹饪的食谱还是要做的锻炼。 您的收藏也可以与朋友分享。

Albo 来自伦敦的应用工作室 The Feel Good Project，该工作室专注于让用户感到灵感和满足的技术，而不是因末日滚动而疲惫不堪。

该应用程序可免费使用，并可通过订阅获得高级功能。 然而，我们不喜欢它在入职期间推动试用订阅的严厉程度。

在 iOS 和 Google Play 上可用。

Coop

美国最近爆发的寄生虫疫情让人们更加仔细地思考他们的食物来自哪里。 从当地种植者和面包师那里购买可能是更安全的选择，对社区也更好，但并不是每个人都有时间在周末去农贸市场。

Coop 的应用程序通过其邻里市场提供了另一种选择，您可以从附近的人那里购买真正的手工制作和本土种植的物品，甚至可以从路边提供新鲜鸡蛋的农舍购买，或者从愿意用他们的物品交换您的物品的邻居那里购买。 这个想法是让商业留在当地，同时帮助人们将自己的花园、田地或工艺品变成额外的收入来源。

在 Coop 上，您可以浏览和发现附近的卖家，关注您最喜欢的卖家，查看他们离您有多远，并通过应用程序的 Stripe 集成向他们购买。 然后，卖家收到订单并准备取货。

在 iOS 和 Google Play 上可用。

PI.FYI 完美不完美

PI.FYI 是一款色彩缤纷但有些混乱的应用程序，它承诺带回“旧互联网”，即你通过朋友网络而不是算法找到推荐。 该应用程序诞生于一份狂热的时事通讯，已经存在了几年，但仍然给人一种新鲜和现代的感觉，非常像它所希望成为的社交媒体的替代品。

在 PI.FYI 中，您可以跟踪您的兴趣、分享您的品味，并按类别或“场景”（例如音乐、奇思妙想、复古和文学）浏览，以查找您的社区、阅读有趣的文章、列出列表、收集本地推荐以及与朋友一起玩游戏。 该应用程序本身就散发着复古气息，就好像它是在互联网还不太完善的时候开发的一样。

在 iOS 和 Google Play 上可用。

信

好吧，这可能不像通过鸽子邮件分享信件那么有趣，但笔友应用程序 Lettre 也包含了数字格式蜗牛邮件的乐趣。 这款写信应用程序可让您与通过该应用程序发现的世界各地的笔友或与您已知的电子邮件地址的任何人建立新的友谊。 不幸的是，目前信件是通过应用程序或电子邮件以数字方式发送的，但该公司的常见问题解答表明，它正在考虑未来的邮寄选项，这将非常有趣。

仅适用于 iOS。

沙发时间

虽然 Sofa Time 不是一款全新的应用程序，但它是接续最近关闭的 TV Time 应用程序的几款应用程序之一。 该应用程序具有易于使用、整洁的界面，用于跟踪您正在观看的电影和电视节目、组织您的观看列表、发现接下来要播放的内容以及获取有关新版本的提醒。

虽然 Sofa Time 的评论部分还无法与 TV Time 的论坛相媲美，但该应用程序的社交元素为社区的发展留下了空间，因为它支持对 GIF 或图像与文本进行反应，并包含内置翻译功能以支持全球受众。

在 iOS 和 Google Play 上可用。

事物书

ThingsBook 是韩国互联网巨头 Naver 美国子公司推出的一款新的专注于写作的应用程序，它很难说是一个独立的项目，但它为社交媒体的未来提供了一个有趣的前提。 ThingsBook 不是末日滚动，而是提供了一个灵活的空间，您可以在其中捕捉您关心的内容，无论是通过日记、记录想法，还是将书籍、旅行、膳食、爱好和目标等内容收集到您可以重新访问和扩展的结构化列表中。

该公司解释说，该应用程序的目的不是关注“稍纵即逝的趋势”，而是成为“你是谁和你所爱的活记录”。

在 iOS 和 Google Play 上可用。

压制花瓣

应用程序还是艺术项目？ 压制花瓣两者兼而有之。 该应用程序是设计师辛西娅·陈 (Cynthia Chen) 的独立作品，它可以将你散步时发现的花朵照片转化为压缩标本，就像你在“复古植物期刊”中找到的标本一样。 该应用程序会自动保存您发现花朵的位置以及日期和时间，将您的自然漫步变成互动体验。 它还通过名称（学名和俗名）来识别花。

您可以尝试使用该应用免费按压两朵花，然后支付 4.99 美元的一次性费用来解锁完整体验。 这可能是一个有趣的应用程序，可以吸引您的孩子外出，因为除了徒步旅行之外，它还为他们提供了其他事情可做。

仅适用于 iOS。

心情更快

我们很喜欢那些构建良好的单一用途应用程序。 Nick Leith 的 Moods Faster 就是一个完美的例子，因为它提供了一种记录你的情绪的方法，只需轻按两次即可在 Apple Health 中进行跟踪 - 一次选择情绪，第二次保存它。

您可以选择记录当前心情或当天的整体心情，还可以选择添加有关记录时的背景和情绪的信息。 在设置中，您可以根据自己的心情选择不同的配色方案，尽管有些是付费的。

每月 1.95 美元，对于任何出于心理健康目的定期跟踪情绪和情绪的人来说，这是一个合理的订阅价格。

仅适用于 iOS。

激活健身

Activate Fitness 最初的定位是鼓励孩子锻炼身体，但最近将其赚取屏幕时间的应用程序扩展到了整个家庭，坦率地说，这让它变得更好。 （孩子们会讨厌他们的父母不使用这个。 另外，它可能会将户外时间或锻炼变成孩子们心目中可怕的苦差事，从而达不到目的。）

对于成年人来说，该应用程序可以让您实现自己的个人目标，例如在您完成当天的步骤之前不要进行末日滚动。

仅适用于 iOS。
